The test image shows a longitudinally cut tomato stem with prominent dark brown/black discoloration of the internal vascular tissue and pith. The outer cortex remains green. This is classic vascular wilt symptomology. Top candidates: Verticillium_Wilt, Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato.

Now viewing one reference image for Verticillium_Wilt:

The reference Verticillium Wilt image shows external leaf yellowing/wilting symptoms (a different presentation than my test image). However, the test image shows the classic **internal diagnostic** of vascular wilt: a longitudinally cut tomato stem with dark brown/black discoloration of the vascular tissue and pith, with the outer cortex still green.

This internal stem vascular discoloration is the textbook field diagnostic for Verticillium Wilt. While Bacterial Canker could also show pith browning, the extent and pattern of dark vascular streaking running the full length of the cut stem is most characteristic of Verticillium Wilt.
